## Bio

*[Adriano
Rutz]{about="wd:Q97455964" property="wdt:P31" resource="wd:Q5" typeof="schema:Person"}*
is a [postdoctoral
researcher]{about="wd:Q1125292" property="wdt:P31" resource="wd:Q28640" typeof="schema:Occupation"}
at [ETH
Zurich]{about="wd:Q11942" property="wdt:P31" resource="wd:Q875538" typeof="schema:CollegeOrUniversity"},
where he develops [computational]{about="wd:Q104595152"} and [analytical
methods]{about="wd:Q4751159"} for [metabolomics]{about="wd:Q12149006"}. His
[research]{about="wd:Q42240"} focuses on the [chemistry]{about="wd:Q2329"} of
[Life]{about="wd:Q3"} and the [metabolites]{about="wd:Q407595"} found in
[organisms]{about="wd:Q7239"}. He trained in [pharmaceutical
sciences]{about="wd:Q7180763s"} and [phytochemistry]{about="wd:Q640068"}, worked
at Tradall SA ([Bacardi Group]{about="wd:Q685395"}), and completed his
[PhD]{about="wd:Q752297"} at the [University of Geneva]{about="wd:Q503473"}.

His work uses [mass spectrometry]{about="wd:Q180809"} to determine which
[chemical compounds]{about="wd:Q11173"} are present in a
[sample]{about="wd:Q485146"}, and aims to make this
[knowledge]{about="wd:Q9081"} [open]{about="wd:Q232932"} and
[reusable]{about="wd:Q115999420"}. He is a core contributor to the [LOTUS
initiative](https://doi.org/10.7554/eLife.70780), and works across [data
science]{about="wd:Q2374463"}, chemistry, and [biology]{about="wd:Q420"}. His
computational work connects research data across systems using open principles,
designing architectures that adapt smoothly across different tools and
environments.
